headline: Ralph Loop Lets Claude Code Work Through the Night
lede: A plugin for Anthropic's command-line coding tool creates autonomous development loops that keep running long after the developer closes the laptop. Named after the perpetually-trying Simpsons character, Ralph Loop has accumulated over 156,000 installs by solving a mundane but costly problem: AI coding assistants that stop too soon.
body:
Every developer who has used an AI coding assistant knows the rhythm: you write a prompt, the model works for a while, then stops and announces completion. You check. It is 60% done. You re-prompt. The cycle continues, each iteration requiring a human to push the next domino. Ralph Loop breaks that cycle. The plugin, officially distributed by **Anthropic** through its Claude Code plugin directory, intercepts the *stop hook* — a shell command that fires when Claude Code exits — and instead of letting the session end, re-feeds the original prompt and relaunches. Every file change and every git commit made during the previous run survives, so each iteration builds forward rather than starting cold.

The name comes from Ralph Wiggum, the Simpsons character whose defining trait is stubborn, oblivious persistence. That philosophy is the point. Where standard Claude Code sessions terminate when the model *believes* it has finished, Ralph keeps iterating until a user-defined success criterion — typically passing tests — is actually satisfied. The loop's exit condition is external and objective, not the model's own confident-but-premature declaration.

The practical result is illustrated by the quoted post from @damianplayer: a half-finished workflow left running at bedtime, six autonomous iterations completed by morning, the developer having written not a single additional line. That kind of overnight delegation was previously the province of expensive, purpose-built *autonomous agents* — systems with their own orchestration layers. Ralph produces something similar using Claude Code's existing infrastructure.

The deeper shift is in the *human-in-the-loop* calculus. Most agentic coding tools still require a human to re-prompt after each stumble; Ralph's loop removes that friction entirely for tasks with clear, automated success signals. The caveat is proportional: the quality of the loop depends entirely on the quality of the tests and acceptance criteria the developer writes before walking away. A vague prompt yields vague iterations, and the model can circle industriously without making real progress. The technique rewards developers who invest in good test coverage — and punishes those who don't.

concepts.definition: A shell command configured to execute automatically when a process exits. In the Claude Code context, Ralph Loop registers a stop hook so that each time a coding session ends, the hook script fires, checks whether the task is complete, and restarts the session if not.

Anthropic's command-line AI coding tool that runs inside a developer's terminal, reads and edits files directly, and executes shell commands. It is distinct from Claude's chat interface — it operates on a local repository rather than in a browser window.

A software system that pursues a goal over multiple steps without requiring human input between each step. In AI coding, an autonomous agent can read code, write changes, run tests, observe the results, and revise — all without a human re-prompting.

A system design pattern in which a human must review, approve, or redirect an AI's output before the next step proceeds. Removing the human from the loop means the AI can act continuously, which is faster but requires more trust in its judgment and error-handling.

The use of AI models to autonomously perform multi-step software development tasks — reading files, writing code, running tests, and iterating on failures — with minimal human intervention between steps.

repos.summary: A community implementation of the Ralph Wiggum autonomous-loop technique for Claude Code, featuring intelligent exit detection. It wraps Claude Code sessions in a loop that re-launches after each exit until a success condition is met, preserving file state and git history between runs. The project predates or parallels the official Anthropic plugin and served as a reference implementation for the technique.
